decisions.reason: The smallest architecture has one input channel, one layer, one output channel and cutoff zero: lift (2), layer weight/bias (2), real zero-frequency multiplier (1), and output weight/bias (2), totaling seven scalar parameters. Thus S=1 gives an empty class and the original unconditional selector-existence premise is inconsistent. The repair retains every integer S>=1, assumes a Borel empirical minimizer only for nonempty classes, defines the empty selector set explicitly and uses inf(empty)=+infinity. No finite-budget or asymptotic claim is dropped.

The zero function and a nonzero tent are 1-Lipschitz but are not injective inverse maps on [0,1]; no forward operator is supplied. The Example and Verification correctly assert only a scalar prediction lower bound. Correcting inverse map to function in the title repairs this presentation defect while preserving the full claim and proof.

As written, m>=1 permits m=3/2. With p=s=R=1, theta=(1/2)e_2 and eta=0, the ellipsoid sum equals one, truncation keeps only coordinate 1, and the error 1/2 exceeds (m+1)^(-1)=2/5. Verification 1.2 needs j>m to imply j>=m+1, which requires integer m. The repair explicitly makes m a positive integer in the Example and Given, preserving the intended first-m-coordinate mesh and the full stated estimate.

The triangle inequality gives the displayed estimate, including m=1, zero noise, and zero truth. Delta is necessarily nonnegative whenever the assumed norm bound has an instance.
